title: Why a chimney draws smoke upwards
examples: Why does smoke go up the chimney?
Why does a taller chimney draw better?
Why does a cold chimney smoke into the room?

explain.say: A fire heats the air and smoke above it. Hot gas is much less dense than the cold air outside, because its particles are moving fast and spread out.

draw.text: Why a chimney draws smoke upwards

explain.say: The column of hot gas inside the chimney weighs less than an equal column of cold air outside. The heavier outside air pushes in at the bottom and shoves the light hot gas up, like a cork pushed up through water.
The push is bigger than the weight of the hot gas plus the drag of the chimney walls, so the smoke rises steadily. This upward pull is called the draught.

A taller or hotter chimney has a bigger difference in weight between inside and outside, so it draws more strongly. A cold chimney full of cold air may push smoke back into the room until it warms up.

faq.q: Why does smoke go up the chimney?
faq.a: Smoke and hot gases are less dense than the cold air around the house. The denser outside air pushes in at the bottom and forces the light hot gas up and out of the top.
asks: Why does a fire need a chimney?

faq.q: What is a draught in a chimney?
faq.a: The draught is the upward flow of air and smoke through a chimney, caused by the hot gas inside being lighter than the cold air outside. It also pulls fresh air into the fire.

faq.q: Why does a taller chimney draw better?
faq.a: The taller the column of hot gas, the bigger the weight difference between it and the same height of cold outside air, so the push upwards is stronger.
asks: Why are factory chimneys so tall?

faq.q: Why does a cold chimney smoke into the room?
faq.a: A cold chimney is filled with cold, heavy air that resists the smoke. Until the flue warms up there is little or no draught, so smoke can spill out.
asks: Why does my fireplace smoke when I first light it?

faq.q: Why does a chimney help a fire burn?
faq.a: As hot gases rise out of the top, fresh air full of oxygen is pulled in at the bottom, feeding the fire.
asks: How does a chimney feed the fire with air?

facts: The chimney draught, or stack effect, comes from the difference in density between hot flue gas and cooler outside air.
Taller chimneys produce a stronger draught because the column of light hot gas is longer.

quiz.say: Why does a taller chimney give a stronger draught?
quiz.show: Why does a taller chimney give a stronger draught?

options.show: A longer hot column means a bigger weight difference
options.say: A longer hot column means a bigger weight difference

options.say: It is closer to the clouds

quiz.why: The upward push depends on how much lighter the hot column is than the same height of cold air, and a taller column adds more difference.
